# With AI

## Limitations first. The Bundibugyo report, 2026

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="40%"}
- **The live report** on the Bundibugyo virus disease outbreak puts its
  limitations before the methods, in bullets, most consequential first
- The dashboard's limits were on a page few reached. This report leads
  with them
- **The feedback** is that this is off-putting
- How should we warn?

> Every estimate is a model-based extrapolation under strong assumptions,
> not a measurement.
>
> *Abbott, Sherratt, Brand and Funk, 2026*
:::
::: {.column width="60%"}
![](../figures/comms-shot-bvd-limits.png){height="600px"
fig-align="center"
fig-alt="The Limitations section of the live BVDOutbreakSize report. A
heading, one sentence on how they are grouped, an expand toggle, and the
first bullets under Data and what it can support"}

::: {.attribution}
[BVDOutbreakSize analysis page](https://epiforecasts.io/BVDOutbreakSize/stable/analysis#Limitations),
v1.18.0, screenshot 12 September 2026
:::

## Making it visible

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="40%"}
- **A bot account.** Agent work goes out from a second GitHub login, so
  `git log` tells you who did most of it
- **A disclosure line** in the Bundibugyo analysis README and on the
  limitations slide of the WHO call about it
- **A prompts page** with the brief and the steers
- **A bio drafted by the bot.** My conference bio for JuliaCon came from
  seabbs-bot, "who has a very suspiciously high opinion of me, so take
  it with a pinch of salt"

## Checking what it wrote

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="40%"}
- **114 claims** pulled out of one deck by a second agent workflow, each
  tested against git and the GitHub API
- **67 needed changing**
- "530 pull requests" was GitHub's latest issue number. The count was
  353
- 712 of 1,371 merged bot pull requests carried no review, so "reviewed
  by me" became "about half"
:::
::: {.column width="60%"}
![](../figures/comms-claims.png){width="100%"
fig-alt="A single bar of 114 claims, 67 marked changed and 47 marked stood"}

::: {.attribution}
[seabbs/how-I-llm](https://github.com/seabbs/how-I-llm) commits
`8c7e834` and `1fceb9a`, August 2026
:::
:::

## seabbs-review-bot

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="40%"}
- **A GitHub App.** It reviews each pull request I or my bot open, and
  again when either of us asks
- A pull request is a proposed change that someone reads before it lands
- **213 pull requests** reviewed since 17 August 2026. Each review ends
  "Not a human review"
- I fix what it gets right, say which findings I reject and why, and
  check each against the source myself
- It has caught real bugs. It has also been wrong from its own truncated
  greps
:::
::: {.column width="60%"}
![](../figures/comms-shot-review-bot.png){width="100%"
fig-alt="The GitHub App page for seabbs-review-bot. A robot avatar, the
name, and the line Automated reviews of @seabbs and @seabbs-bot work"}

::: {.attribution}
[github.com/apps/seabbs-review-bot](https://github.com/apps/seabbs-review-bot),
created 17 August 2026 · count from the GitHub search API,
`reviewed-by:app/seabbs-review-bot`, 12 September 2026 · the rules from
my own `CLAUDE.md`, the standing instructions my agents read
:::
